financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (standalone) basis, same filing/period as GROUP row -- see GROUP row's notes for shared context (segment verification, leverage ratios, borrowings-field scope). Company revenue +31% YoY to Rs.7,246.531mn (2025: Rs.5,547.804mn); Cost of Sales +29% to Rs.5,500.296mn; Gross Profit +36% to Rs.1,746.235mn. Company carries an unusually large 'Share of Profit/(loss) of Equity Accounted Investees' line at STANDALONE level (-Rs.3,602.025mn 2026, -Rs.4,213.085mn 2025) -- Company applies the equity method to its investment in subsidiaries/associates in its own standalone accounts (an LKAS 27 policy option), which is why Company PAT (-Rs.5,041.916mn) ties EXACTLY to the Group's 'Equity holders of the Company' attribution (-Rs.5,041.916mn) -- not a coincidence or extraction error, a genuine feature of this filing's accounting policy. operating_profit = printed 'Results from operating activities': Rs.596.978mn (2026) vs Rs.811.091mn (2025), -26% YoY -- Company Other Income swung from +Rs.330.309mn (2025) to -Rs.9.317mn (2026), the main driver of the operating-profit decline even as Gross Profit grew. Company PBT improved (loss narrowed) from -Rs.5,323.460mn to -Rs.5,041.916mn (Rs.281.544mn narrower, ~5.3%), driven by the smaller Share-of-equity-accounted-investee loss (-Rs.3,602.025mn vs -Rs.4,213.085mn, Rs.611.060mn improvement) more than offsetting the weaker operating result and higher Net Finance Cost (-Rs.2,036.869mn vs -Rs.1,921.466mn, +6%). No tax expense either period at Company level. shares_in_issue = 212,625,000, same register as Group. EPS cross-check: -5,041,916 / 212,625 = -23.71, ties. Identity check: total_liabilities (9,474.214+69,931.004=79,405.218) + total_equity (113,525.824) = 192,931.042, ties printed Total Assets 192,931.042mn exactly.

Brown & Company PLC (BRWN), diversified conglomerate (LOLC Group-affiliated -- top 3 shareholders, Seylan Bank/LOLC Holdings collateral 28.22%, LOLC Holdings PLC 24.50%, HNB/LOLC Holdings 14.11%, combined 66.83%, per Note 10.3), FYE 31 March. GROUP (consolidated) basis. Q1 FY2026/27 ('Three Months Ended 30 June 2026') vs Q1 FY2025/26 (three months ended 30 June 2025) comparative, both explicitly labelled 'Quarter ended 30th June' on the face Income Statement (page 2) -- genuine same-quarter YoY compare; first quarter of FYE 31 March so no QoQ distinction needed. SEGMENT NOTE (Note 7, page 10): 7 reportable segments -- Trading, Manufacturing & Engineering, Investments, Plantation, Leisure, Real Estate, Others -- plus an 'Adjustments' (inter-segment elimination) column and Group Total. Column mapping independently verified: Revenue row sums to Group Total (13,586,563+6,686,401+2,522+18,952,989+3,302,736+146,442+12,546-363,501=42,326,698, ties printed 42,326,697 to rounding) and PBT row likewise sums to Group Total (743,911+540,004-3,942,482-18,466-3,071,301-109,933-57,080-923,410=-6,838,757, ties printed -6,838,756) -- both independent cross-checks passed, so segment figures below are used with confidence. operating_profit = printed face-P&L subtotal 'Results from operating activities' (page 2): Rs.5,687.276mn (2026) / Rs.3,321.976mn (2025), i.e. before Net Finance Cost and Share of Profit of Equity Accounted Investees. REVENUE DRIVER: Group revenue +31% YoY to Rs.42,326.697mn (2025: Rs.32,275.341mn, +Rs.10,051.356mn). Segment attribution of the increase: Plantation segment (largest segment, 44.8% of Group revenue) grew 50.9% to Rs.18,952.989mn (2025: Rs.12,562.399mn), contributing Rs.6,390.590mn -- ~63.6% of the ENTIRE revenue increase on its own; Manufacturing & Engineering grew 40.4% to Rs.6,686.401mn (2025: Rs.4,760.661mn), contributing Rs.1,925.740mn (~19.2% of the increase); Trading grew 15.8% to Rs.13,586.563mn (2025: Rs.11,736.871mn), contributing Rs.1,849.692mn (~18.4%); Leisure grew 12.3% to Rs.3,302.736mn; Real Estate grew 15.5% to Rs.146.442mn; Investments segment revenue COLLAPSED 99.0% to just Rs.2.522mn (2025: Rs.260.862mn, -Rs.258.340mn); Others fell 6.0% to Rs.12.546mn. Gross profit grew even faster (+67% to Rs.10,503.711mn, 2025: Rs.6,289.686mn) as Cost of Sales grew only 22% -- Group gross margin expanded from 19.5% to 24.8%. PROFIT DRIVER: despite the operating improvement (Results from operating activities +71% to Rs.5,687.276mn), Group PBT remained deeply negative at -Rs.6,838.756mn, though this is a Rs.1,179.789mn NARROWING versus the -Rs.8,018.545mn loss in 2025 (loss narrowed ~14.7%), because Net Finance Cost of -Rs.12,384.235mn (2025: -Rs.11,578.086mn, +7% YoY) exceeds the entire operating profit -- per Note 9, the Group's own disclosed Interest Cover ratio is just 0.47x (operating profit covers under half of net finance costs) and Debt/Equity ratio is 69.72%, both filing-disclosed leverage/solvency metrics corroborating this structural driver. At the SEGMENT level, the improvement in the headline loss is NOT uniform: Investments segment losses narrowed from -Rs.6,010.599mn (2025) to -Rs.3,942.482mn (2026), an improvement of Rs.2,068.117mn (~34.4% narrower) -- this segment carries very large Other Income (Rs.3,208.978mn, 2026) against very large Expenses (-Rs.7,152.650mn, 2026), consistent with fair-value/finance-cost-heavy investment-holding activity rather than trading revenue (segment revenue is negligible at Rs.2.522mn) -- BUT Leisure segment losses WORSENED sharply, from -Rs.1,913.584mn (2025) to -Rs.3,071.301mn (2026), a Rs.1,157.717mn DETERIORATION (+60.5% worse), a genuine negative driver partly offsetting the Investments-segment improvement. Manufacturing & Engineering swung from a LOSS of -Rs.888.825mn (2025) to a PROFIT of +Rs.540.004mn (2026), a Rs.1,428.829mn positive swing -- a genuine operational turnaround in this segment. Real Estate segment loss widened from -Rs.62.010mn to -Rs.109.933mn (+77.3% worse), small in absolute terms. Tax expense rose sharply, +138% YoY to Rs.658.571mn (2025: Rs.276.465mn), despite the Group-level pretax loss -- this is consistent with segment-level taxable profits existing in Trading (income tax expense -97,329 vs -7,014, i.e. +Rs.90.315mn) and Manufacturing & Engineering (-230,976 vs -30,767, i.e. +Rs.200.209mn) segments even as other segments post losses not immediately tax-deductible at Group level -- a genuine tax-driver worth flagging, not an anomaly. BALANCE SHEET: total_liabilities = Non-Current (130,056.743) + Current (414,103.373) = 544,160.116mn, ties EXACTLY to the segment note's own printed Group Total Liabilities (544,160,116th). short_term_borrowings = sum of three separate current-liability lines -- 'Loans and Borrowings' (9,054.909) + 'Short Term Borrowings' (50,636.061) + 'Bank Overdrafts' (21,534.942) = 81,225.912mn -- all conventional short-term interest-bearing debt; DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES 'Loans from Related Parties' (current, Rs.43,598.419mn) and 'Amounts due to Related Parties' (Rs.191,908.402mn), both very large related-party balances kept separate per line-item discipline (see gaps_note -- material and worth flagging, not a conventional bank-borrowings gap). long_term_borrowings = Non-current 'Loans and Borrowings' only (44,018.815mn), excludes Lease Liabilities (15,905.936) and non-current Loans from Related Parties (755.503). trade_payables = 'Trade and Other Payables' (96,492.171mn) as printed, a combined line. capex (5,142.877mn) = 'Acquisition of Property, Plant and Equipment/Biological Assets/Investment Properties', a single combined cash-flow line, gross (not netted against Rs.26.439mn disposal proceeds), no further breakdown given. shares_in_issue = 212,625,000 (Note 2). EPS cross-check: -5,041,916 / 212,625 (both '000) = -23.71, ties exactly. Identity check: total_liabilities (544,160.116) + total_equity (266,322.490) = 810,482.606, ties printed Total Assets 810,482.606mn exactly.

interim_updates.note_text: Brown & Company PLC (BRWN), a LOLC Group-affiliated diversified conglomerate (Trading, Manufacturing & Engineering, Investments, Plantation, Leisure, Real Estate, Others), narrowed its Group net loss 9.6% YoY to Rs.7,497.33mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), from Rs.8,295.01mn a year earlier, on Group revenue up 31% YoY to Rs.42,326.70mn (2025: Rs.32,275.34mn, +Rs.10,051.36mn). By segment (Note 7, Segment reporting, independently cross-checked to the printed Group Total): the Plantation segment, the Group's largest at 44.8% of revenue, drove nearly two-thirds of the entire revenue increase -- revenue +50.9% YoY to Rs.18,952.99mn (2025: Rs.12,562.40mn), contributing Rs.6,390.59mn of the Rs.10,051.36mn Group increase (~63.6%). Manufacturing & Engineering added a further Rs.1,925.74mn (+40.4% to Rs.6,686.40mn, ~19.2% of the increase) and Trading a further Rs.1,849.69mn (+15.8% to Rs.13,586.56mn, ~18.4%); Leisure grew 12.3% to Rs.3,302.74mn and Real Estate 15.5% to Rs.146.44mn, while the Investments segment's own revenue collapsed 99.0% to just Rs.2.52mn (2025: Rs.260.86mn) as it is fundamentally a fair-value/finance-cost-driven holding segment, not a trading one. Group gross margin expanded from 19.5% to 24.8% as Cost of Sales grew only 22% against 31% revenue growth, lifting Results from operating activities 71% YoY to Rs.5,687.28mn (2025: Rs.3,321.98mn). Despite this operating improvement, Group PBT stayed deeply negative at Rs.(6,838.76)mn -- a Rs.1,179.79mn (14.7%) narrowing from Rs.(8,018.55)mn -- because Net Finance Cost of Rs.12,384.24mn (2025: Rs.11,578.09mn, +7% YoY) exceeds the entire operating profit; the filing's own disclosed Interest Cover ratio of just 0.47x and Debt/Equity ratio of 69.72% (Note 9) corroborate finance costs, not operations, as the binding constraint on profitability. The improvement in the headline loss was NOT uniform across segments: Investments segment losses narrowed Rs.2,068.12mn (34.4% narrower, from Rs.(6,010.60)mn to Rs.(3,942.48)mn PBT) on lower fair-value losses against large Other Income of Rs.3,208.98mn, but Leisure segment losses WORSENED sharply, by Rs.1,157.72mn (60.5% worse, from Rs.(1,913.58)mn to Rs.(3,071.30)mn PBT), partly offsetting the Investments-segment gain. Manufacturing & Engineering swung from a Rs.(888.83)mn PBT LOSS to a Rs.540.00mn PBT PROFIT, a genuine Rs.1,428.83mn operational turnaround, while Real Estate's small loss widened 77.3% (to Rs.(109.93)mn from Rs.(62.01)mn). Income Tax Expense rose 138% YoY to Rs.658.57mn (2025: Rs.276.47mn) despite the Group-level pretax loss, consistent with segment-level taxable profits in Trading (tax +Rs.90.32mn YoY) and Manufacturing & Engineering (tax +Rs.200.21mn YoY) even as loss-making segments generate no offsetting tax credit at Group level. Basic Loss per Share improved to Rs.(23.71) from Rs.(25.04) a year earlier. At Company (standalone parent) level, revenue also grew 31% YoY to Rs.7,246.53mn (2025: Rs.5,547.80mn) and gross profit +36% to Rs.1,746.24mn, but Results from operating activities FELL 26% YoY to Rs.596.98mn (2025: Rs.811.09mn) because Other Income swung from +Rs.330.31mn to Rs.(9.32)mn -- the single driver of the Company operating decline despite stronger gross profit. Company PBT loss still narrowed 5.3% (Rs.281.54mn) to Rs.(5,041.92)mn (2025: Rs.(5,323.46)mn), because the Share of Loss of Equity Accounted Investees -- a large standalone-level line reflecting BRWN's equity-method accounting for its subsidiaries in the Company's own books -- improved by Rs.611.06mn (from Rs.(4,213.09)mn to Rs.(3,602.03)mn), more than offsetting the weaker operating result and a 6% rise in Net Finance Cost (to Rs.2,036.87mn from Rs.1,921.47mn). Company PAT of Rs.(5,041.92)mn ties exactly to the Group's 'Equity holders of the Company' loss attribution, a genuine accounting-policy feature (LKAS 27 equity-method option at Company level), not a data error.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the first financial_statements/interim_updates entry for BRWN in this database, no prior quarter collected. Q1 FY2026/27 is the first quarter of BRWN's FYE 31 March financial year, so no QoQ distinction would apply here in any case. The segmental note (Note 7) discloses PBT and revenue by segment for both the current and prior-year quarter (a genuine YoY comparison at segment level, independently cross-checked here: segment Revenue sums to Group Total Rs.42,326,698k vs printed Rs.42,326,697k, and segment PBT sums to Rs.(6,838,757)k vs printed Rs.(6,838,756)k, both within Rs.1k rounding), but does NOT break out the underlying drivers within each segment (e.g. which Plantation sub-crop or Manufacturing & Engineering product line drove the growth) -- a genuine disclosure limit, not an extraction gap. The Investments segment's Rs.3,208.98mn Other Income and Rs.(7,152.65)mn Expenses are not itemised by underlying instrument/investee, so the exact mix of realised vs unrealised fair-value movement within the Rs.2,068.12mn YoY improvement cannot be isolated further. short_term_borrowings and long_term_borrowings as mapped in the financial_statements entry deliberately EXCLUDE two very large related-party funding lines -- 'Loans from Related Parties' (current, Rs.43,598.42mn) and 'Amounts due to Related Parties' (Rs.191,908.40mn) -- which are material (together larger than total conventional borrowings) but kept separate per line-item discipline; the filing itself gives no further detail on the nature/terms of these related-party balances, a genuine disclosure gap worth flagging given their size relative to the Group's Rs.266,322.49mn total equity.
interim_updates.takeaway: BRWN's Group net loss narrowed 9.6% YoY on strong 31% revenue growth concentrated in the Plantation segment (+50.9%, ~63.6% of the total revenue increase) and a genuine operational turnaround in Manufacturing & Engineering (Rs.1,428.83mn PBT swing to profit), but the improvement was capped by two specific, quantified offsets: Net Finance Cost of Rs.12,384.24mn continuing to exceed the entire Rs.5,687.28mn operating profit (Interest Cover just 0.47x per the filing's own disclosure), and a Rs.1,157.72mn deterioration in Leisure segment losses that partly cancelled out a Rs.2,068.12mn improvement in the Investments segment. At Company (standalone) level the improvement came from a different source entirely -- a smaller Share of Loss of Equity Accounted Investees -- masking a 26% decline in the Company's own operating profit. With Debt/Equity at 69.72% and interest cover below 0.5x, BRWN's near-term earnings trajectory remains more sensitive to finance costs and segment-level leverage than to underlying trading momentum, which is otherwise broadly positive across most segments this quarter.

operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.42,326.70mn, +31% YoY (2025: Rs.32,275.34mn); Group net loss narrowed 9.6% YoY to Rs.7,497.33mn (2025: Rs.8,295.01mn); Results from operating activities +71% YoY to Rs.5,687.28mn.
Plantation segment (44.8% of Group revenue) drove ~63.6% of the entire Group revenue increase: revenue +50.9% YoY to Rs.18,952.99mn, contributing Rs.6,390.59mn of the Rs.10,051.36mn Group increase.
Manufacturing & Engineering swung from a Rs.(888.83)mn PBT loss to a Rs.540.00mn PBT profit YoY, a genuine Rs.1,428.83mn operational turnaround; Trading segment revenue +15.8% to Rs.13,586.56mn.
Leisure segment PBT loss WORSENED 60.5% YoY (Rs.1,157.72mn deterioration, to Rs.(3,071.30)mn), partly offsetting a Rs.2,068.12mn (34.4%) narrowing in Investments segment losses.

Group PBT loss narrowed only 14.7% (to Rs.(6,838.76)mn) despite 71% operating profit growth, because Net Finance Cost of Rs.12,384.24mn exceeds the entire operating profit -- disclosed Interest Cover just 0.47x, Debt/Equity 69.72% (Note 9).
Income Tax Expense +138% YoY to Rs.658.57mn despite the Group pretax loss, driven by segment-level taxable profits in Trading (+Rs.90.32mn) and Manufacturing & Engineering (+Rs.200.21mn).

Company (standalone) operating profit fell 26% YoY to Rs.596.98mn as Other Income swung from +Rs.330.31mn to Rs.(9.32)mn, but Company PBT loss still narrowed 5.3% on a Rs.611.06mn improvement in Share of Loss of Equity Accounted Investees.
key_drivers: Plantation segment revenue growth (+50.9% YoY to Rs.18,952.99mn) contributed ~63.6% of the Group's entire Rs.10,051.36mn revenue increase, the single largest driver of top-line growth.

Net Finance Cost of Rs.12,384.24mn (+7% YoY) exceeding the entire Rs.5,687.28mn operating profit is why a 71% operating-profit surge only narrowed the Group PBT loss by 14.7% -- disclosed Interest Cover of 0.47x confirms leverage, not trading performance, is the binding constraint.

Manufacturing & Engineering's Rs.1,428.83mn PBT swing (loss to profit) is the clearest genuine segment turnaround; Leisure's Rs.1,157.72mn PBT deterioration is the main offsetting negative segment driver.

Company-level PBT improvement (Rs.281.54mn narrower loss) was driven by a Rs.611.06mn improvement in Share of Loss of Equity Accounted Investees, not by operating performance, which actually fell 26% YoY on a swing in Other Income from +Rs.330.31mn to Rs.(9.32)mn.
